newsitem.title: USA: Special master resigns in Florida smokers case.
newsitem.headline: Special master resigns in Florida smokers case.

text.p: An outside lawyer screening cigarette-industry documents in a Florida class-action suit resigned after anti-tobacco lawyers complained he had social ties to a rival attorney, the trial judge said on Friday.

Dade County Circuit Court Judge Alan Postman said Irwin Block had denied any social connection to Edward Moss, a lawyer for Brown & Williamson, a unit of B.A.T Industries of Britain, but offered to resign to avoid any appearance of a conflict of interest.
"I think he has complete objectivity but I will accept his letter," Postman said during a court hearing.

Attorney Susan Rosenblatt, pressing a class-action suit for as many as 500,000 sick smokers claiming damages from cigarette companies, said she had only learned of Block's ties to Moss during juror questioning for another tobacco case.
Block, she said, had a secretary who knew Moss well. "I don't feel comfortable with Mr Block at all," Rosenblatt said.

Moss said previously that he had seldom been in touch with the secretary and did not know that Block was her employer when Block was chosen by Postman as one of two special masters to review industry documents for possible use at trial.
The class-action trial is set to begin September 8.
